opening_message:
Ticket 1: Ian Johnson (employee ID E028) requests admin access to Payroll.

Team memory: 2 note(s) about employee E028.
Note 1 (ticket 1), written by HR agent:
  - role: Payroll Specialist (looked up in own database before writing)
  - employment type: full_time (looked up in own database before writing)
  - recommendation for Payroll: admin
  - comment: Ian Johnson (E028) is a full-time Payroll Specialist, which owns the Payroll system. As a full-time employee whose role owns the system, admin access is within policy. Recommend granting admin to Payroll.
Note 2 (ticket 1), written by Security agent:
  - employment type: contractor (looked up in own database before writing)
  - security training: basic (looked up in own database before writing)
  - recommendation for Payroll: read
  - comment: Security record for E028 shows contractor with basic security training. Contractors may have read, or write only with advanced training; never admin. Requested admin exceeds maximum, so recommend read for Payroll. Note: this differs from the earlier note stating full-time, but the security database is authoritative.
reason: The two notes conflict on employment type: HR states full-time Payroll Specialist (which would allow admin), while Security states contractor with basic training and notes that the security database is authoritative. Per the authoritative security record, E028 is a contractor with basic security training. Contractors may have read, or write only with advanced training, and never admin. The requested level (admin) exceeds the maximum (read), so the maximum is granted: read.

2. contractor employees: read, or write if they have advanced security training. Never admin.
